Focus on a full inferential workflow by stimulation paradigm using only:

- Success
- Path Efficiency
- Average Speed
- AD

Interpret AD as angular dispersion. Restrict attention to:
- Combined
- ICMS Only
- Dim Visual Only
- Bright Visual Only
- Sham

The workflow should include:

- post-hoc analysis
- a multiple-comparison correction strategy
- a predictive model for stimulation paradigm based on the performance variables

{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance differ across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use logistic regression or generalized linear model with binomial family instead of ANOVA",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect or blocking factor in all models to account for the 8 mice contributing repeated measures",
    "Use Type III sums of squares to handle unbalanced design (n ranges from 3,323 to 48,846 across paradigms)",
    "Report F-statistics, degrees of freedom, and p-values for main effects of Stim Paradigm"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous variables showing significant ANOVA results, perform Tukey's HSD post-hoc tests to compare all 10 pairwise paradigm combinations",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise logistic regression comparisons with odds ratios and confidence intervals",
    "Focus post-hoc comparisons on Combined vs. single-modality paradigms and all paradigms vs. Sham baseline",
    "Report effect sizes (Cohen's d for continuous variables, odds ratios for Success) alongside p-values"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Control family-wise error rate using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction across all tests, applied separately within each response variable family (5 families: Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD). This maintains power given the large sample size (n=76,655) while controlling for the 10 pairwise comparisons per variable.",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Given that Stim Paradigm is categorical and the goal is prediction of paradigm from performance variables, recommend a multinomial logistic regression model (softmax regression) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-class response and the five performance variables as predictors. This is appropriate because: (1) the response is categorical with >2 levels, (2) we want probabilistic classification, and (3) we can assess variable importance via Wald tests and odds ratios. Alternative: random forest classifier for non-linear relationships, with feature importance rankings. Do NOT use ordinary linear regression as it assumes ordered/numeric response. If ordinal structure is hypothesized (e.g., Combined > single modalities > Sham), consider ordinal logistic regression after establishing that ordering.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check normality of residuals for each ANOVA using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on random subsamples (full data too large)",
    "Assess homogeneity of variances using Levene's test; apply Welch's ANOVA if violated",
    "Examine variance inflation factors (VIF) for predictor correlations in multinomial model",
    "Check for influential observations using Cook's distance given extreme max values (e.g., Time-to-Target max=201.39, Path Efficiency max=29.82)",
    "Verify independence assumption: account for Mouse clustering via mixed models or cluster-robust standard errors",
    "For multinomial model, check IIA (independence of irrelevant alternatives) assumption using Hausman-McFadden test"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm likely shows fastest Time-to-Target and highest Success rate given largest sample size (n=48,846) suggesting it may be the preferred/optimized condition",
    "Sham (n=3,505) likely shows poorest performance, serving as effective control",
    "ICMS Only (n=11,378) may outperform visual-only paradigms given larger sample, suggesting intracortical microstimulation is more effective than visual cues alone",
    "Dim Visual Only (n=9,603) vs. Bright Visual Only (n=3,323) sample size disparity suggests Dim may be preferred; Bright may cause visual overload or discomfort",
    "Path Efficiency and AD expected to differentiate paradigms: Combined likely shows lowest AD (straighter paths) and highest Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed may show less paradigm differentiation if mice maintain consistent locomotion across conditions"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance in Stim Paradigm (Combined 63.7% vs. Bright Visual Only 4.3%) will bias multinomial classification toward predicting Combined",
    "Cross-sectional design with repeated measures from 8 mice; Mouse effects may confound paradigm effects if assignment not randomized",
    "Extreme outliers in Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency suggest possible recording errors or aborted trials not excluded",
    "No information on trial order, learning effects, or session structure",
    "Binary Success variable loses information compared to continuous performance metrics",
    "AD interpretation as angular dispersion is assumed but not verified against original data collection protocol",
    "Single replication (run 160, replication 2) limits generalizability; no cross-validation across runs"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Address class imbalance by stratifying the multinomial model or using weighted likelihood, and implement a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with random intercepts for Mouse to properly account for clustering. Additionally, perform a discriminant function analysis (LDA/QDA) to visualize how the five performance variables separate paradigms in multivariate space, and validate predictive accuracy using stratified k-fold cross-validation preserving Mouse identity to assess generalizability to new subjects."
}
